grammars.text:
dot = /./
dots = /.+/
spaces = /\s+/
non-spaces = /\S+/
words = /\w+/
non-words = /\W+/
bounded-word = /\b\w+\b/
digits = /\d+/
not-newline = /[^\n]+/
line = /[^\r\n\u2028\u2029]*/
line-end = /\r\n|\r|\n|\u2028|\u2029/
letters = /\p{L}+/
letter-marks = /(\p{L}\p{M}*)+/
pictographs = /\p{Extended_Pictographic}+/
anything = /[\s\S]+/
token = /[^\s"]+/
quoted = /"[^"]*"/
lines = (line, line-end)+
spaced-words = (non-spaces, spaces)+
text = (quoted | token | spaces)+

a = "a"
b = "b"
pair = a + b
as = (a)+
listed = (a, ",")+
num = /\d+/
add = expr + "+" + expr
neg = "-" + expr
inc = expr + "++"
expr = add | neg | inc | num

# calc — arithmetic expression grammar, bash `$(( ))` parity.
#
# Precedence (loosest → tightest, matches bash arithmetic / C):
#   comma   ,
#   assign  = += -= *= /= %= &= ^= |= <<= >>=   (right-assoc)
#   ternary ? :                                 (right-assoc)
#   logOr   ||
#   logAnd  &&
#   bitOr   |
#   bitXor  ^
#   bitAnd  &
#   eq      == !=
#   comp    < <= > >=
#   shift   << >>
#   add     + -
#   mul     * / %
#   exp     **                                  (right-assoc)
#   unary   ! ~ +x -x ++x --x x++ x--
#   atom    NUMBER | IDENTIFIER | ( expr )
#
# DIVERGENCE FROM PRIOR calc: `^` was exponent. Now `^` is BITWISE XOR
# and `**` is exponent — matches bash. Update any old tests accordingly.

# ─── Whitespace ──────────────────────────────────────────────
ws = /[ \t\n\r]+/

# ─── Numbers ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Hex first (longest prefix), then octal (only when followed by 0-7
# digits and NOT 8/9/decimal point — disambiguates `09` as decimal,
# not malformed octal), then decimal.
hexNumber = /0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+/
octalNumber = /0[0-7]+(?![0-9.])/
decimalNumber = /(?:\d+(?:\.\d+)?|\.\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?/
number = hexNumber | octalNumber | decimalNumber

# ─── Identifier (variable reference / assignment target) ────
identifier = /[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]*/
varRef = identifier

# ─── Operator literals ──────────────────────────────────────
# Listed longest-first where they share a prefix so cpat's first-match
# commits to the longer form (`<<=` before `<<` before `<=` before `<`).
shlAssign = "<<="
shrAssign = ">>="
addAssign = "+="
subAssign = "-="
mulAssign = "*="
divAssign = "/="
modAssign = "%="
bitAndAssign = "&="
bitOrAssign  = "|="
bitXorAssign = "^="
expOp        = "**"
shlOp        = "<<"
shrOp        = ">>"
logAndOp     = "&&"
logOrOp      = "||"
eqOp         = "=="
neOp         = "!="
leOp         = "<="
geOp         = ">="
incOp        = "++"
decOp        = "--"

# Single-char ops use negative-lookahead so they don't accidentally
# eat the first char of a longer operator at the same position.
# `1 && 2` would otherwise parse as `1 & (& 2)` because `&` matches
# greedily before the alternation reaches `&&`. Same trick the shell
# grammar uses for `arithBitAndOp = /&(?!&|=)/`.
addOp     = /\+(?![+=])/
subOp     = /-(?![-=])/
mulOp     = /\*(?![*=])/
divOp     = /\/(?!=)/
modOp     = /%(?!=)/
bitAndOp  = /&(?![&=])/
bitOrOp   = /\|(?![|=])/
bitXorOp  = /\^(?!=)/
ltOp      = /<(?![<=])/
gtOp      = />(?![>=])/
notOp     = /!(?!=)/
bitNotOp  = "~"
assignOp  = /=(?!=)/

question  = "?"
colon     = ":"
comma     = ","

# ─── Operator groups ────────────────────────────────────────
mulModOp  = mulOp | divOp | modOp
addSubOp  = addOp | subOp
shiftOp   = shlOp | shrOp
compOp    = leOp | geOp | ltOp | gtOp
equalityOp = eqOp | neOp

compoundAssignOp =
    shlAssign | shrAssign
  | addAssign | subAssign | mulAssign | divAssign | modAssign
  | bitAndAssign | bitOrAssign | bitXorAssign
anyAssignOp = compoundAssignOp | assignOp

# ─── Punctuation ─────────────────────────────────────────────
openParen  = "("
closeParen = ")"

# ─── Group (parenthesized expression) ───────────────────────
group = openParen + ws? + expr + ws? + closeParen

# ─── Unary prefix ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Each prefix binds the entire expr to its right; cpat's PEG ordered
# alternation in `expr` resolves the precedence (these listed near
# the top → tightest binding).
preIncExpr   = incOp    + ws? + expr
preDecExpr   = decOp    + ws? + expr
unaryPlus    = addOp    + ws? + expr
unaryMinus   = subOp    + ws? + expr
logNotExpr   = notOp    + ws? + expr
bitNotExpr   = bitNotOp + ws? + expr

# ─── Postfix ────────────────────────────────────────────────
postIncExpr = expr + incOp
postDecExpr = expr + decOp

# ─── Binary expressions ─────────────────────────────────────
expExpr     = expr + ws? + expOp       + ws? + expr
mulExpr     = expr + ws? + mulModOp    + ws? + expr
addExpr     = expr + ws? + addSubOp    + ws? + expr
shiftExpr   = expr + ws? + shiftOp     + ws? + expr
compExpr    = expr + ws? + compOp      + ws? + expr
eqExpr      = expr + ws? + equalityOp  + ws? + expr
bitAndExpr  = expr + ws? + bitAndOp    + ws? + expr
bitXorExpr  = expr + ws? + bitXorOp    + ws? + expr
bitOrExpr   = expr + ws? + bitOrOp     + ws? + expr
logAndExpr  = expr + ws? + logAndOp    + ws? + expr
logOrExpr   = expr + ws? + logOrOp     + ws? + expr

# ─── Ternary ────────────────────────────────────────────────
ternaryExpr = expr + ws? + question + ws? + expr + ws? + colon + ws? + expr

# ─── Assignment ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Visitor verifies the LHS is a varRef (lvalue) — grammar accepts any
# expr to mirror bash's runtime error behavior rather than a parse
# failure when the LHS is non-assignable.
assignExpr = expr + ws? + anyAssignOp + ws? + expr

# ─── Comma ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
commaExpr = expr + ws? + comma + ws? + expr

# ─── expr (Expression-promoted) — tightest first ───────────
# Order matters: cpat's PEG tries alternatives left-to-right; for
# binary operators, listing TIGHTER ones first establishes precedence
# via expression promotion. Right-associative rules carry `right`.
expr = preIncExpr
     | preDecExpr
     | postIncExpr right
     | postDecExpr right
     | unaryPlus
     | unaryMinus
     | logNotExpr
     | bitNotExpr
     | expExpr right
     | mulExpr
     | addExpr
     | shiftExpr
     | compExpr
     | eqExpr
     | bitAndExpr
     | bitXorExpr
     | bitOrExpr
     | logAndExpr
     | logOrExpr
     | ternaryExpr right
     | assignExpr right
     | commaExpr
     | group
     | number
     | varRef

# ─── Top level ──────────────────────────────────────────────
calc = ws? + expr + ws?

# date_expr — GNU-coreutils-style "date input formats" grammar.
#
# A date expression is a whitespace-separated SEQUENCE of items. Each
# item either sets ABSOLUTE fields (a calendar date, a time of day, a
# timezone, an epoch stamp) or accumulates a RELATIVE offset (`+3 days`,
# `2 weeks ago`) or a weekday adjust (`next monday`). The visitor folds
# the whole sequence into one `DateItems` accumulator; `fold.ts` then
# resolves it against `now`.
#
# This mirrors how `src/calc/grammar.cpat` and `src/jq/grammar.cpat` are
# structured: regex/string leaves, `+` sequence, `|` ordered choice, `?`
# optional, `(item, sep)+` repetition. There is NO operator precedence
# here — a date expression is a flat list, so we use a flat repetition
# (`items`) instead of calc's expression-promotion.
#
# PEG ordered choice: `item`'s alternatives are listed MOST-SPECIFIC
# first so a longer form commits before a shorter prefix can match
# (e.g. an ISO datetime before a bare calendar date; a timezone-bearing
# time before a bare time).
#
# Timezones: `Z`/`UT`/`GMT`/`UTC`, the common US abbrevs, numeric
# `±HH[:]MM` offsets, AND full IANA `Area/Location` names (e.g.
# `America/New_York`, or GNU's `TZ="…"` prefix) — the latter resolved to
# a DST-correct offset at the instant via `Intl` in the folder.

# ─── Whitespace (also swallows a leading comma, e.g. "May 16, 2026") ──
ws = /(?:[ \t\n\r]+|,[ \t\n\r]*)+/

# ─── Primitive numeric leaves ───────────────────────────────────────
sign      = /[+-]/
year4     = /\d{4}/
mon2      = /\d{1,2}/
day2      = /\d{1,2}/
intNum    = /\d+/
fracSec   = /\.\d+/

# ─── Month names (long + 3-letter abbrev, case-insensitive) ─────────
# cpat regex leaves don't accept a trailing `/i` flag, so case-folding
# uses inline `(?i:...)` groups throughout this grammar.
monthName =
  /(?i:january|jan|february|feb|march|mar|april|apr|may|june|jun|july|jul|august|aug|september|sep|october|oct|november|nov|december|dec)\b/

# ─── Day-of-week names (long + abbrev, case-insensitive) ────────────
# Trailing `s` allowed for the `next 2 fridays` plural form.
dowName =
  /(?i:sunday|sun|monday|mon|tuesday|tue|wednesday|wed|thursday|thu|friday|fri|saturday|sat)s?\b/

# ─── Timezone tokens ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Named zones map to fixed offsets in the visitor. Numeric offsets
# (`Z`, `+05:00`, `-0800`) are parsed structurally.
tzNamed   = /(?i:UTC|GMT|UT|EST|EDT|CST|CDT|MST|MDT|PST|PDT)\b/
tzZulu    = /[Zz]/
tzNumeric = /[+-]\d{2}:?\d{2}/
# IANA `Area/Location` name (requires a `/`, so it never steals a bare
# word). Validated + resolved to a DST-correct offset via Intl in the
# folder; an unknown name fails the parse. Allows 3-part names
# (`America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires`) and `+`/`-` (`Etc/GMT+5`).
tzIana    = /[A-Za-z]+(?:\/[A-Za-z0-9_+-]+)+/
# Named zones / numeric offsets are distinct shapes; tzIana (has a `/`)
# is the catch-all, tried last.
tzOffset  = tzZulu | tzNumeric | tzNamed | tzIana
# GNU's `TZ="America/New_York"` prefix form (quoted or bare). Matched as
# one token; the visitor strips `TZ=` and any quotes.
tzAssign  = /(?i:TZ)=(?:"[^"]+"|\S+)/

# ─── Epoch: @SECONDS (optionally fractional) ────────────────────────
epochItem = /@\d+(?:\.\d+)?/

# ─── Time of day: HH:MM[:SS[.fff]] [am|pm] [tz] ─────────────────────
hour2     = /\d{1,2}/
min2      = /\d{2}/
sec2      = /\d{2}/
ampm      = /(?i:am|pm|a\.m\.|p\.m\.)\b/
clockSecs = ":" + sec2 + fracSec?
timeCore  = hour2 + ":" + min2 + clockSecs?
timeOfDay = timeCore + (ws? + ampm)? + (ws? + tzOffset)?

# ─── ISO 8601 combined date+time ────────────────────────────────────
isoDate     = year4 + "-" + mon2 + "-" + day2
# Date/time separator is `T`, `t`, or a single space. A trailing zone
# may be glued (`...00Z`) or space-separated (`... UTC`), so allow `ws?`.
isoDateTime = isoDate + /[Tt ]/ + timeCore + (ws? + tzOffset)?

# ─── Calendar dates (several spellings) ─────────────────────────────
# YYYY-MM-DD and YYYY/MM/DD (4-digit year leads).
dashYMD  = year4 + "-" + mon2 + "-" + day2
slashYMD = year4 + "/" + mon2 + "/" + day2
# MM/DD/YYYY (US, year trails).
slashMDY = mon2 + "/" + day2 + "/" + year4
# DD-Mon-YYYY (e.g. 16-May-2026).
dMonY    = day2 + "-" + monthName + "-" + year4
# "Month D[ ,] [YYYY]" and "D Month [YYYY]" — year optional.
monthDY  = monthName + ws + day2 + (ws + year4)?
dMonthY  = day2 + ws + monthName + (ws + year4)?

calendarDate = isoDateTime | dashYMD | slashYMD | slashMDY | dMonY | monthDY | dMonthY

# ─── Day-of-week with optional this/next/last + optional count ──────
thisKw = /(?i:this)\b/
nextKw = /(?i:next)\b/
lastKw = /(?i:last)\b/
dowKindKw = thisKw | nextKw | lastKw
# `next 2 fridays` — a count between the kind and the day name.
dowItem = (dowKindKw + ws)? + (intNum + ws)? + dowName

# ─── Relative units ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Singular/plural handled in the visitor by stem matching.
unitWord =
  /(?i:years?|yrs?|months?|fortnights?|weeks?|days?|hours?|hrs?|minutes?|mins?|seconds?|secs?)\b/
agoKw = /(?i:ago)\b/
# `[+-]?[N] UNIT [ago]` — the count is optional (`+ day` ≡ `+1 day`).
relUnitItem = (sign + ws?)? + (intNum + ws)? + unitWord + (ws + agoKw)?
# `next/last/this WEEK` etc. — kind + unit, no count.
relKindItem = dowKindKw + ws + unitWord

# ─── Bare keywords ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
nowKw       = /(?i:now)\b/
todayKw     = /(?i:today)\b/
tomorrowKw  = /(?i:tomorrow)\b/
yesterdayKw = /(?i:yesterday)\b/
noonKw      = /(?i:noon)\b/
midnightKw  = /(?i:midnight)\b/
keywordItem = nowKw | todayKw | tomorrowKw | yesterdayKw | noonKw | midnightKw

# ─── One item (ordered: most-specific / longest-prefix first) ───────
# epoch → calendar (incl. ISO datetime) → time-of-day → relative
# (kind+unit, then count+unit) → day-of-week → bare keywords.
# `relKindItem` precedes `dowItem` so `next week` is a relative item,
# not a (failed) weekday; `dowItem` precedes nothing that would steal
# `next monday`. Keywords last — they're the shortest, most ambiguous.
item =
    tzAssign
  | epochItem
  | calendarDate
  | timeOfDay
  | relKindItem
  | relUnitItem
  | dowItem
  | keywordItem

# ─── Item sequence ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
items = (item, ws)+

# ─── Top level ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
dateExpr = ws? + items + ws?

# find — predicate-expression grammar.
#
# Input shape: the encoder in `./encoder.ts` takes the shell's
# tokenized args + the `_meta` channel and produces a single string
# where:
#   - Structural tokens (keywords, operators, terminators, grouping)
#     are bare and whitespace-separated.
#   - Every value is either a bareword (if its source was a single
#     bareword wordPart) or a double-quoted token (if the source had
#     a quoted / expansion / brace-list part).
#   - Inside `-exec ... ;` / `-exec ... +` the encoder always quotes
#     args (even barewords), so the only bare tokens between -exec
#     and its terminator are the terminator itself.
#
# Structure: the grammar produces a FLAT LIST of items (atoms +
# `-o` markers + `-a`/`-and` no-op markers). The visitor groups
# items by `-o` boundaries, ANDs items within each group, and ORs
# the groups together. This avoids left-recursive infix grammar
# and keeps the cpat side small.
#
# Precedence (visitor):
#   - `-not` / `!` (prefix on a single atom — handled in `notExpr`)
#   - implicit AND between adjacent atoms (visitor combines)
#   - `-o` / `-or` (lowest — visitor splits chain on these)

# ─── Whitespace ──────────────────────────────────────────────
ws = /[ \t\n\r]+/

# ─── Tokens ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Standard double-quoted string. Visitor unescapes `\\` and `\"`.
quoted = /"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"/

# A bareword is any non-whitespace, non-quote, non-paren run. Listed
# AFTER the keyword rules in alternations so cpat tries the keyword
# literals first and `bareword` is the fallback for everything else.
# Includes `;` and `+` so a value like `foo+bar` parses as one token
# — `-exec` terminator disambiguation is handled by the encoder
# always quoting exec args.
bareword = /[^"\s()]+/

# ─── Structural single-char tokens ──────────────────────────
openParen  = "("
closeParen = ")"
semi       = ";"
plus       = "+"

# ─── Operator keywords ──────────────────────────────────────
notKw  = "-not"
bangKw = "!"
notOp  = notKw | bangKw

andKw  = "-and"
aKw    = "-a"
andOp  = andKw | aKw

orKw   = "-or"
oKw    = "-o"
orOp   = orKw | oKw

# ─── Predicate keywords ─────────────────────────────────────
maxdepthKw = "-maxdepth"
mindepthKw = "-mindepth"
typeKw     = "-type"
nameKw     = "-name"
inameKw    = "-iname"
pathKw     = "-path"
ipathKw    = "-ipath"
regexKw    = "-regex"
iregexKw   = "-iregex"
sizeKw     = "-size"
emptyKw    = "-empty"

# ─── Action keywords ────────────────────────────────────────
printKw  = "-print"
print0Kw = "-print0"
deleteKw = "-delete"
execKw   = "-exec"

# ─── Value (predicate argument) ─────────────────────────────
# Accepts a quoted token OR a bareword. The encoder guarantees that
# values originating from quoted / expansion / brace-list parts arrive
# as `quoted`, so a value that happens to spell a keyword is
# unambiguous — the grammar isn't in keyword-position here.
value = quoted | bareword

# ─── Predicates ─────────────────────────────────────────────
pMaxdepth = maxdepthKw + ws + value
pMindepth = mindepthKw + ws + value
pType     = typeKw     + ws + value
pName     = nameKw     + ws + value
pIname    = inameKw    + ws + value
pPath     = pathKw     + ws + value
pIpath    = ipathKw    + ws + value
pRegex    = regexKw    + ws + value
pIregex   = iregexKw   + ws + value
pSize     = sizeKw     + ws + value
pEmpty    = emptyKw

predicate = pMaxdepth
          | pMindepth
          | pType
          | pName
          | pIname
          | pPath
          | pIpath
          | pRegex
          | pIregex
          | pSize
          | pEmpty

# ─── Actions ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# -exec collects (quoted)+ until a bare `;` or `+`. The encoder
# always quotes -exec args, so the only bareword between -exec and
# the terminator is the terminator itself.
execArg     = quoted
execArgList = (execArg, ws trim)+
execTerm    = semi | plus
aExec       = execKw + ws + execArgList + ws + execTerm

aPrint  = printKw
aPrint0 = print0Kw
aDelete = deleteKw

action = aExec | aPrint0 | aDelete | aPrint

# ─── Grouping ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# `( ... )` wraps an inner chainItems list so precedence can be
# overridden. The visitor descends transparently into the group's
# inner chain.
group = openParen + ws? + chainItems + ws? + closeParen

# ─── Negation ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# `-not` / `!` is a prefix that binds to a single atom (the atom
# rule includes notExpr so `-not -not -name foo` works via right
# recursion).
notExpr = notOp + ws + atom

# ─── Atom ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
atom = group | notExpr | action | predicate

# ─── Chain items ────────────────────────────────────────────
# The visitor reads this list, splits on orMarker, AND-joins atoms
# within each segment, OR-joins segments. andMarker is consumed by
# the grammar (so `-a` / `-and` parse cleanly) but contributes no
# semantics — implicit AND is the default between atoms.
orMarker  = orOp
andMarker = andOp
chainItem = orMarker | andMarker | atom

chainItems = (chainItem, ws trim)+

# ─── Top level ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# pathArg is handled by `src/tools/find.ts` BEFORE encoding — it
# peels off the leading non-keyword positional and only the
# expression body is fed to cpat. So findExpr here is just an
# optional chainItems wrapped in optional whitespace.
findExpr = ws? + chainItems? + ws?

# Glob pattern grammar — the structured form of a shell glob, including
# extended globbing (`shopt -s extglob`). The Glob matcher parses a
# pattern with this grammar and walks the resulting AST into a RegExp.
#
# Only patterns that contain an extglob opener route through here; plain
# `*` / `?` / `[…]` globs keep their original fast string scan. So this
# grammar always parses at least one extglob group, but it also has to
# understand every ordinary glob metachar that can sit alongside one.
#
# The five extglob operators each take a `|`-separated list and may nest:
#   ?(list) *(list) +(list) @(list) !(list)
# Nesting is handled by ordinary grammar recursion (`itemIn` → `extGroup`)
# rather than a Block delimiter — a raw depth-scan would miscount escaped
# parens, whereas the `escaped` rule (tried before any literal) consumes
# `\(` / `\)` / `\|` as literals so they never affect group structure.

# ─── Leaf metacharacters ────────────────────────────────────────────
# `escaped` is first in every item list so `\X` is always a literal.
escaped     = /\\./
doubleStar  = "**"
star        = "*"
question    = "?"

# Character class `[…]` / `[!…]` as one escape-aware regex: a leading `]`
# (or `!]`) is part of the class (`[]]`, `[!]]`), `\]` stays inside, and
# the class ends at the first unescaped `]`.
charClass   = /\[!?\]?(?:\\.|[^\]])*\]/

# `extOpen` is a negative-lookahead sentinel (operator char glued to `(`):
# a literal run stops before it so the operator starts a group instead.
extOpen     = /[?*+@!]\(/
extOp       = /[?*+@!]/
open        = "("
close       = ")"

# ─── Literal runs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A literal char is anything not handled above. Two variants: top-level
# treats `(` `)` `|` as ordinary chars; inside a group `(`/`)` bound
# (nested) groups and `|` divides alternatives, so all three are excluded
# there. Every char is guarded by `!extOpen` so a run never swallows the
# operator char of a following extglob group.
litTopChar  = /[^*?\[\\]/
litInChar   = /[^*?\[\\|()]/
litTopUnit  = !extOpen + litTopChar
litInUnit   = !extOpen + litInChar
litTopRun   = (litTopUnit)+
litInRun    = (litInUnit)+

# ─── Items ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# extGroup is tried first so an `op(` commits to a group before the
# operator char is read as a literal.
itemTop = extGroup | escaped | charClass | doubleStar | star | question | litTopRun
itemIn  = extGroup | escaped | charClass | doubleStar | star | question | litInRun

# ─── Extglob group ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# `extGroup` recurses through `itemIn`, so nested groups Just Work without
# a delimiter scan. An empty alternative (`@(a|)`) is allowed.
extAlt   = (itemIn)*
extAlts  = (extAlt, "|")+
extGroup = extOp + open + extAlts + close

# ─── Top level ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
globPattern = (itemTop)+

# ─── Whitespace ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Whitespace also swallows `#`-to-end-of-line comments, so they may
# appear anywhere inter-token whitespace is allowed. `#` inside a string
# is safe — dqString tokenizes the whole `"..."` before ws is consulted.
ws = /(?:[ \t\n\r]+|#[^\n]*)+/

# ─── Reserved keywords ──────────────────────────────────────
trueKw  = "true"
falseKw = "false"
nullKw  = "null"
andKw   = "and"
orKw    = "or"
ifKw    = "if"
thenKw  = "then"
elifKw  = "elif"
elseKw  = "else"
endKw   = "end"
tryKw   = "try"
catchKw = "catch"
asKw    = "as"
defKw     = "def"
reduceKw  = "reduce"
foreachKw = "foreach"
labelKw   = "label"
breakKw   = "break"
moduleKw  = "module"
importKw  = "import"
includeKw = "include"

# ─── Identifier (excludes reserved keywords) ────────────────
identifier = /(?!(?:true|false|null|and|or|if|then|elif|else|end|try|catch|as|def|reduce|foreach|label|break|import|include|module)\b)[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*/

# A bareword that DOESN'T exclude keywords. jq allows reserved words in two
# positions where there's no ambiguity: object keys (`{if: 1}`) and variable
# names (`$then`, `$foreach`). Both are anchored by a preceding `{`/`,`/`:` or
# `$`, so letting a keyword through here can't be mistaken for the keyword's
# statement form.
bareWord = /[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*/

# ─── Numbers ────────────────────────────────────────────────
number   = /(?:\d+(?:\.\d+)?|\.\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?/

# ─── Double-quoted strings (with interpolation) ──────────────
# A jq string is a `"`-delimited run of literal chunks and `\(expr)`
# interpolations. A flat token regex CANNOT model this: an interpolation
# may itself contain a nested string (`"x\(.a + "y")"`), whose interior
# `"` would prematurely close a regex-based token. So `dqString` is a
# structured atom — `strChunk` matches a literal run (any `\X` escape
# except the `\(` that opens an interpolation, plus ordinary non-quote
# chars), and `interpolation` recurses into `expr` between `\(` and `)`.
# Because the self-reference sits in the MIDDLE (never at the start/end),
# the Expression classifier treats dqString as an Atom — same shape as
# `group`. The visitor evaluates it structurally (see visitor/atoms.ts).
strChunk      = /(?:\\[^(]|[^"\\])+/
interpStart   = /\\\(/
interpolation = interpStart + ws? + expr + ws? + closeParen
strPart       = interpolation | strChunk
strParts      = (strPart)+
dqString      = "\"" + strParts? + "\""

# ─── Operator literals ──────────────────────────────────────
# `|=` is the update-assignment op, so a bare `|` must not eat it.
pipeOp  = /\|(?!=)/
commaOp = ","
# `//=` is the alt-assignment op, so a bare `//` must not eat its `=`.
altOp   = /\/\/(?!=)/
eqOp    = "=="
neOp    = "!="
leOp    = "<="
geOp    = ">="
ltOp    = "<"
gtOp    = ">"
# Each bare arithmetic op needs a negative lookahead so it doesn't
# consume the leading char of its compound-assignment variant
# (`+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, `%=`). Without these, `.x += 5` would
# match `+` here, leave `= 5` dangling, and addExpr would fail —
# but cpat's expression promotion doesn't reliably backtrack to
# assignExpr from a half-matched addExpr.
addOp   = /\+(?!=)/
subOp   = /-(?!=)/
mulOp   = /\*(?!=)/
divOp   = /\/(?![\/=])/
modOp   = /%(?!=)/
optOp   = "?"

multOp   = mulOp | divOp | modOp
addSubOp = addOp | subOp
compOp   = eqOp | neOp | leOp | geOp | ltOp | gtOp

# ─── Punctuation ─────────────────────────────────────────────
openParen      = "("
closeParen     = ")"
openSqBracket  = "["
closeSqBracket = "]"
openBracket    = "{"
closeBracket   = "}"
dot            = "."
recurseKw      = ".."
colon          = ":"
semicolon      = ";"
varSigil       = "$"
formatAt       = "@"

# ─── Literal atoms ──────────────────────────────────────────
literal = number | trueKw | falseKw | nullKw

# ─── Variable reference ($x) ────────────────────────────────
# Variable names may be reserved words (`$then`, `$foreach`, `$label`); the
# `$` sigil removes any ambiguity with the keyword's statement form. An
# optional `::suffix` names a data module's binding (`$d::d`).
varName  = /[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(?:::[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)?/
variable = varSigil + varName

# ─── Format reference (@base64, etc.) ───────────────────────
formatName = identifier
formatRef  = formatAt + formatName
formatExpr = formatRef + ws? + dqString
formatAtom = formatRef

# ─── Identity / field path ──────────────────────────────────
# Bare `.` is identity, but `.5` is the number 0.5 — so identity must NOT
# match a `.` that begins a leading-dot number literal. (A `.` before `[`,
# a letter, or another `.` still matches: those are index/field/recurse.)
identity  = /\.(?![0-9])/
fieldName = identifier
fieldPath = dot + fieldName
# `."quoted key"` — sugar for `.["quoted key"]`, for keys that aren't
# bare identifiers. The dqString may interpolate, like `.[ ]` does.
quotedFieldPath = dot + dqString

# ─── Group ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Committed at `(` — the only rule that starts an expression atom with a
# bare paren (reduce/foreach/def parens follow keywords; computedKey lives
# in object-key position). Kills the superlinear re-read of `(`-runs
# (docs/cpu-runaway-audit.md K1: 1000 parens ≈ 0.6 s and growing).
group = openParen ~/ ws? + expr + ws? + closeParen

# ─── Array construction ─────────────────────────────────────
arrayExpr = openSqBracket + ws? + expr? + ws? + closeSqBracket

# ─── Object construction ────────────────────────────────────
# Object keys may be reserved words unquoted (`{if: 1, and: 2}`).
objectKeyName    = bareWord
quotedKey        = dqString
computedKey      = openParen + ws? + expr + ws? + closeParen
# A `$var: value` entry keys on the variable's (string) VALUE — `$k: 1` is
# `{ ($k): 1 }`. Listed last so `$x` with no colon still falls to the shorthand.
objectKey        = objectKeyName | quotedKey | computedKey | variable
objectEntryPair  = objectKey + ws? + colon + ws? + exprNoComma
objectShorthand  = objectKeyName
objectVarShort   = variable
# `{"a"}` is shorthand for `{"a": .a}` (and `{"\(f)"}` for the interpolated
# key). Tried after `objectEntryPair` so `"a": v` still parses as a pair.
objectStrShort   = quotedKey
objectEntry      = objectEntryPair | objectVarShort | objectStrShort | objectShorthand
objectComma      = ws? + commaOp + ws?
objectEntries    = (objectEntry, objectComma trim)+
objectExpr       = openBracket + ws? + objectEntries? + ws? + closeBracket

# ─── if / then / elif / else / end ─────────────────────────
elseIfBranch   = elifKw + ws + expr + ws + thenKw + ws + expr
elseIfBranches = (elseIfBranch, ws)+
elseBranch     = elseKw + ws + expr
ifExpr = ifKw + ws + expr + ws + thenKw + ws + expr + ws? + elseIfBranches? + ws? + elseBranch? + ws? + endKw

# ─── try / catch ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Unlike `if`/`reduce`/`foreach` (which are closed by `end`/`)`), `try` and
# its `catch` handler have NO trailing delimiter. In jq's precedence table
# `try`/`catch` bind TIGHTER than every infix operator, so `1 + try 2 catch 3
# + 4` is `1 + (try 2 catch 3) + 4` (= 7) and `try a catch b | c` is
# `(try a catch b) | c`. We get that by referencing `expr` DIRECTLY at each
# rule's tail — cpat then classifies `try`/`catch` as tight PREFIX operators
# (the same idiom as unary `-`), so the body and handler bind an operand
# tighter than `+`/`|`/`,`/`//` instead of swallowing them.
catchClause = ws + catchKw + ws + tightExpr
tryExpr     = tryKw + ws + tightExpr + catchClause?

# ─── label / break ───────────────────────────────────────────
# `label $out | BODY` establishes a named breakpoint; `break $out`
# inside BODY cuts BODY's output stream at that point. As in jq, `label`
# is a lowest-precedence binder whose BODY greedily extends over `,` and
# `|` (so `label $o | .[] | …, break $o` is all one body — no parens).
#
# The greediness comes from hiding the `expr` reference behind the named
# `labelBody` rule, exactly like `defBody` does for `def`: when a rule
# references `expr` DIRECTLY at its tail, cpat classifies it as a prefix
# operator and binds the operand tightly; when the reference is wrapped
# in a sub-rule, the rule is a greedy atom (like `group`/`defExpr`) whose
# inner `expr` consumes maximally. breakExpr is a plain atom.
labelBody = ws? + expr
labelExpr = labelKw + ws + variable + ws? + pipeOp + labelBody
breakExpr = breakKw + ws + variable

# ─── Destructuring patterns ──────────────────────────────────
# A binding target after `as` is a `patternTerm`: one or more `pattern`s
# separated by the `?//` alternative-destructuring operator. A `pattern`
# is a variable, an array pattern, or an object pattern — the array/object
# forms recurse into `pattern`, so the self-reference is always nested
# inside `[ ]` / `{ }` (an Atom in the pattern Expression, like `group`
# in `expr`). Object entries support `$x` shorthand (binds `.x`),
# `key: pattern`, `"str": pattern` (interpolated), and `(expr): pattern`
# (computed). The visitor walks these structurally (see visitor/destructure.ts).
destructAltOp  = "?//"
patComma       = ws? + commaOp + ws?
patternList    = (pattern, patComma trim)+
arrayPat       = openSqBracket + ws? + patternList? + ws? + closeSqBracket
# Object-pattern keys may be reserved words (`{as: $x}`). The `$name: pat`
# form (`objPatVarPair`) is jq's bind-and-recurse: it binds `$name` to `.name`
# AND matches `pat` against `.name` (e.g. `{$b: [$c, $d]}`).
objPatKeyName  = bareWord
objPatKey      = objPatKeyName | dqString | computedKey
objPatPair     = objPatKey + ws? + colon + ws? + pattern
objPatVarPair  = variable + ws? + colon + ws? + pattern
objPatEntry    = objPatVarPair | objPatPair | variable
objPatEntries  = (objPatEntry, patComma trim)+
objectPat      = openBracket + ws? + objPatEntries? + ws? + closeBracket
pattern        = variable | arrayPat | objectPat
destructAltSep = ws? + destructAltOp + ws?
patternTerm    = (pattern, destructAltSep trim)+

# ─── reduce / foreach ────────────────────────────────────────
reduceExpr  = reduceKw + ws + expr + ws + asKw + ws + patternTerm + ws? + openParen + ws? + expr + ws? + semicolon + ws? + expr + ws? + closeParen
foreachExtractPart = ws? + semicolon + ws? + expr
foreachExpr = foreachKw + ws + expr + ws + asKw + ws + patternTerm + ws? + openParen + ws? + expr + ws? + semicolon + ws? + expr + foreachExtractPart? + ws? + closeParen

# ─── def — user function ─────────────────────────────────────
defParam      = variable | identifier
defParamSep   = ws? + semicolon + ws?
defParamList  = (defParam, defParamSep trim)+
defParamGroup = openParen + ws? + defParamList + ws? + closeParen
defName       = identifier
defStatement  = defKw + ws + defName + ws? + defParamGroup? + ws? + colon + ws? + expr + ws? + semicolon
defBody       = ws? + expr
defExpr       = defStatement + defBody

# ─── Module directives (import / include / module) ──────────
# A program may be prefixed by directives: `module {meta};`, then
# `import "path" as ns {meta}?;` / `import "path" as $data {meta}?;`, then
# `include "path" {meta}?;`. Each carries the rest of the program as a greedy
# body (the `def`/`defBody` idiom), so `import "a" as foo; BODY` nests as
# importExpr(directive, BODY). `as ns` (identifier) is a function module;
# `as $data` (variable) is a JSON data import. The optional trailing object is
# the directive metadata (`{search:"./"}`).
importName  = variable | identifier
importDir   = importKw + ws + dqString + ws + asKw + ws + importName + ws? + objectExpr? + ws? + semicolon
includeDir  = includeKw + ws + dqString + ws? + objectExpr? + ws? + semicolon
moduleDir   = moduleKw + ws? + objectExpr + ws? + semicolon
importExpr  = importDir + defBody
includeExpr = includeDir + defBody
moduleExpr  = moduleDir + defBody

# ─── Builtin / user-fn calls ────────────────────────────────
# Same exclusion as `identifier`, plus an optional `::name` namespace suffix
# for imported-module functions (`foo::bar`). A single token so the visitor
# keeps reading `builtinName`'s `.value` ("foo::bar").
builtinName     = /(?!(?:true|false|null|and|or|if|then|elif|else|end|try|catch|as|def|reduce|foreach|label|break|import|include|module)\b)[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(?:::[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)?/
builtinArgSep   = ws? + semicolon + ws?
builtinArgList  = (expr, builtinArgSep trim)+
builtinArgGroup = openParen + ws? + builtinArgList + ws? + closeParen
builtinCall     = builtinName + builtinArgGroup?

# ─── Postfix steps (shared) ─────────────────────────────────
fieldStep    = dot + fieldName
fieldStepStr = dot + dqString
indexStep    = openSqBracket + ws? + expr + ws? + closeSqBracket
sliceStep    = openSqBracket + ws? + expr? + ws? + colon + ws? + expr? + ws? + closeSqBracket
iterateStep  = openSqBracket + ws? + closeSqBracket
optStep      = optOp

# ─── Postfix accesses (in expr) ─────────────────────────────
# `ws?` before each step: jq's lexer skips whitespace between tokens, so a
# postfix access may be separated from its operand by spaces —
# `if … end []`, `.a [0]`, `.a .b` are all valid.
fieldAccess    = expr + ws? + fieldStep
fieldAccessStr = expr + ws? + fieldStepStr
indexAccess    = expr + ws? + indexStep
sliceAccess    = expr + ws? + sliceStep
iterateAccess  = expr + ws? + iterateStep
optionalAccess = expr + ws? + optStep

# Dot-bracket sugar: an optional `.` may precede a bracket step, so
# `.a.[0]` / `.a.[1:2]` / `.a.[]` mean the same as `.a[0]` etc. Same visitor
# as the dot-less forms — the middle `dot` node is ignored (base is
# children[0], step is the last child).
dotIndexAccess   = expr + ws? + dot + indexStep
dotSliceAccess   = expr + ws? + dot + sliceStep
dotIterateAccess = expr + ws? + dot + iterateStep

# ─── Assignment operators ───────────────────────────────────
# Listed longest-first where prefixes overlap. `plainAssignOp` uses
# negative lookahead so a bare `=` doesn't get eaten when followed
# by another `=` (compEx `==`).
altAssignOp   = "//="
updateOp      = "|="
plusAssignOp  = "+="
minusAssignOp = "-="
mulAssignOp   = "*="
divAssignOp   = "/="
modAssignOp   = "%="
plainAssignOp = /=(?!=)/

anyAssignOp = altAssignOp | updateOp | plusAssignOp | minusAssignOp
            | mulAssignOp | divAssignOp | modAssignOp | plainAssignOp

# ─── Unary minus ────────────────────────────────────────────
unaryExpr = subOp + ws? + expr

# ─── Binary expressions (in expr) ───────────────────────────
mulExpr    = expr + ws? + multOp   + ws? + expr
addExpr    = expr + ws? + addSubOp + ws? + expr
compExpr   = expr + ws? + compOp   + ws? + expr
andExpr    = expr + ws? + andKw    + ws? + expr
orExpr     = expr + ws? + orKw     + ws? + expr
altExpr    = expr + ws? + altOp    + ws? + expr
commaExpr  = expr + ws? + commaOp  + ws? + expr
pipeExpr   = expr + ws? + pipeOp   + ws? + expr
assignExpr = expr + ws? + anyAssignOp + ws? + expr
# `E as PAT | BODY`. cpat sees the leading and trailing `expr` and classifies
# this as a BINARY operator whose "operator" is `as PAT |` — so the source and
# body are its two operands, at `asExpr`'s (loose) precedence. Right-associated
# so chained binders nest correctly: `a as $x | b as $y | body` is
# `a as $x | (b as $y | body)`.
asExpr     = expr + ws  + asKw + ws + patternTerm + ws? + pipeOp + ws? + expr

# ─── exprNoComma duplicates (no commaExpr) ──────────────────
fieldAccessNc    = exprNoComma + ws? + fieldStep
fieldAccessStrNc = exprNoComma + ws? + fieldStepStr
indexAccessNc    = exprNoComma + ws? + indexStep
sliceAccessNc    = exprNoComma + ws? + sliceStep
iterateAccessNc  = exprNoComma + ws? + iterateStep
optionalAccessNc = exprNoComma + ws? + optStep
dotIndexAccessNc   = exprNoComma + ws? + dot + indexStep
dotSliceAccessNc   = exprNoComma + ws? + dot + sliceStep
dotIterateAccessNc = exprNoComma + ws? + dot + iterateStep
unaryExprNc      = subOp + ws? + exprNoComma
mulExprNc        = exprNoComma + ws? + multOp   + ws? + exprNoComma
addExprNc        = exprNoComma + ws? + addSubOp + ws? + exprNoComma
compExprNc       = exprNoComma + ws? + compOp   + ws? + exprNoComma
andExprNc        = exprNoComma + ws? + andKw    + ws? + exprNoComma
orExprNc         = exprNoComma + ws? + orKw     + ws? + exprNoComma
altExprNc        = exprNoComma + ws? + altOp    + ws? + exprNoComma
pipeExprNc       = exprNoComma + ws? + pipeOp   + ws? + exprNoComma
assignExprNc     = exprNoComma + ws? + anyAssignOp + ws? + exprNoComma
asExprNc         = exprNoComma + ws  + asKw + ws + patternTerm + ws? + pipeOp + ws? + exprNoComma

# ─── tightExpr duplicates — accesses/primaries, NO infix binaries ──
# The operand level for `try`/`catch` (see the try/catch section). Same
# expression-promotion idiom as `exprNoComma`, but the alternation omits every
# infix binary (`* / % + - == and or = // , |`, `as|`) so a body/handler binds
# only a primary/postfix term (unary `-` kept for `try -.`). Each access rule
# self-references `tightExpr` so cpat's left-recursion resolves within THIS
# promoted pattern (referencing `expr`/`exprNoComma` here would not parse).
fieldAccessT      = tightExpr + ws? + fieldStep
fieldAccessStrT   = tightExpr + ws? + fieldStepStr
indexAccessT      = tightExpr + ws? + indexStep
sliceAccessT      = tightExpr + ws? + sliceStep
iterateAccessT    = tightExpr + ws? + iterateStep
optionalAccessT   = tightExpr + ws? + optStep
dotIndexAccessT   = tightExpr + ws? + dot + indexStep
dotSliceAccessT   = tightExpr + ws? + dot + sliceStep
dotIterateAccessT = tightExpr + ws? + dot + iterateStep
unaryExprT        = subOp + ws? + tightExpr

# ─── expr (Expression-promoted) — tightest first ───────────
expr = optionalAccess
     | fieldAccess
     | fieldAccessStr
     | dotIterateAccess
     | dotSliceAccess
     | dotIndexAccess
     | iterateAccess
     | sliceAccess
     | indexAccess
     | unaryExpr
     | mulExpr
     | addExpr
     | compExpr
     | andExpr
     | orExpr
     | assignExpr right
     | altExpr
     | commaExpr
     | pipeExpr
     | asExpr right
     | group
     | arrayExpr
     | objectExpr
     | dqString
     | ifExpr
     | tryExpr
     | reduceExpr
     | foreachExpr
     | labelExpr
     | breakExpr
     | defExpr
     | importExpr
     | includeExpr
     | moduleExpr
     | recurseKw
     | formatExpr
     | formatAtom
     | builtinCall
     | quotedFieldPath
     | fieldPath
     | variable
     | identity
     | literal

# ─── exprNoComma — same alts minus commaExpr (with Nc binaries) ────
exprNoComma = optionalAccessNc
            | fieldAccessNc
            | fieldAccessStrNc
            | dotIterateAccessNc
            | dotSliceAccessNc
            | dotIndexAccessNc
            | iterateAccessNc
            | sliceAccessNc
            | indexAccessNc
            | unaryExprNc
            | mulExprNc
            | addExprNc
            | compExprNc
            | andExprNc
            | orExprNc
            | assignExprNc right
            | altExprNc
            | pipeExprNc
            | asExprNc right
            | group
            | arrayExpr
            | objectExpr
            | dqString
            | ifExpr
            | tryExpr
            | reduceExpr
            | foreachExpr
            | labelExpr
            | breakExpr
            | defExpr
            | recurseKw
            | formatExpr
            | formatAtom
            | builtinCall
            | quotedFieldPath
            | fieldPath
            | variable
            | identity
            | literal

# ─── tightExpr — same atoms, accesses/unary only (no infix binaries) ──
tightExpr = optionalAccessT
          | fieldAccessT
          | fieldAccessStrT
          | dotIterateAccessT
          | dotSliceAccessT
          | dotIndexAccessT
          | iterateAccessT
          | sliceAccessT
          | indexAccessT
          | unaryExprT
          | group
          | arrayExpr
          | objectExpr
          | dqString
          | ifExpr
          | tryExpr
          | reduceExpr
          | foreachExpr
          | labelExpr
          | breakExpr
          | defExpr
          | recurseKw
          | formatExpr
          | formatAtom
          | builtinCall
          | quotedFieldPath
          | fieldPath
          | variable
          | identity
          | literal

# ─── Top level ──────────────────────────────────────────────
filter = ws? + expr + ws?

# POSIX Basic Regular Expressions, with GNU extensions.
#
# Defining property: most metacharacters are LITERAL unless preceded
# by `\`. Group is `\(...\)`, alternation is `\|`, one-or-more is
# `\+`, zero-or-one is `\?`, bounded quantifier is `\{n,m\}`. `*`,
# `.`, `^`, `$`, and `[...]` work the same as in ERE/PCRE.
#
# Char classes (`[...]`) are tokenised as one opaque match — the
# visitor parses the body using the shared char-class helper rather
# than expressing it in the grammar. The internal rules of `[...]`
# (POSIX classes, ranges, leading-`]` literal) are stateful in a way
# that's awkward to express declaratively; one regex literal + a
# focused visitor is cleaner.
#
# Rule names are stable — the visitor dispatches on them — so don't
# rename without updating `src/shell/regex/visitors/bre.ts`.

# ─── Top level ─────────────────────────────────────────────
bre = breAlternation

# ─── Alternation ───────────────────────────────────────────
# `\|` separates sequences. Empty alternatives are allowed (matches
# real BRE behaviour) by making breSequence's atom list optional.
breAlternation = breSequence + (breAltTail)*
breAltTail     = breAltSep + breSequence
breAltSep      = /\\\|/

# ─── Sequence ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# One sequence is zero or more atom-with-quantifier slots. The `*`
# (zero-or-more) is what lets `\|\|` parse as three empty
# alternatives, matching real BRE.
breSequence = (breAtomQ)*

# ─── Atom + optional quantifier suffix ─────────────────────
# Anchors aren't quantifier-eligible in real BRE (a quantifier after
# `^` is a syntax error / undefined); we accept the quantifier
# grammatically and let the visitor decide whether to attach it. In
# practice no quantifier sneaks past `^`/`$` because the visitor
# treats anchors as atoms and ignores any following quantifier slot.
breAtomQ = breAtom + breQuantSuffix?

# Order matters — most-specific first. Group (`\(`) must beat the
# generic backslash-escape rule, brackets must be tried before the
# bare literal-char fallback.
breAtom = breGroup
        | breCharClass
        | breAnchorStart
        | breAnchorEnd
        | breDot
        | breEscapedAtom
        | breLiteralChar

# ─── Group ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
breGroup      = breGroupOpen + breAlternation + breGroupClose
breGroupOpen  = /\\\(/
breGroupClose = /\\\)/

# ─── Char class — opaque token, visitor parses the body ────
# Regex anatomy:
#   \[                                  opening bracket
#   \^?                                 optional negation
#   \]?                                 optional literal `]` at position 0 (POSIX rule)
#   (?:\[:[a-z]+:\]|\\.|[^\]])*         body: POSIX class OR `\X` OR non-`]`
#   \]                                  closing bracket
# The POSIX-class alternative `\[:name:\]` is listed FIRST so the
# inner `]` of `[:alpha:]` doesn't terminate the outer class — without
# this special case, `[[:alpha:]]` would match only `[[:alpha:]` and
# leave the trailing `]` dangling.
breCharClass = /\[\^?\]?(?:\[:[a-z]+:\]|\\.|[^\]])*\]/

# ─── Anchors ───────────────────────────────────────────────
breAnchorStart = "^"
breAnchorEnd   = "$"

# ─── Dot ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
breDot = "."

# ─── Backslash-led atoms ───────────────────────────────────
# Listed most-specific first. The visitor dispatches on the matched
# leaf node's name so it knows which kind of escape this is.
breEscapedAtom = breBackref
               | breWordBoundaryAlias
               | breWordBoundary
               | breNonWordBoundary
               | breClassDigit
               | breClassWord
               | breClassSpace
               | breClassNotDigit
               | breClassNotWord
               | breClassNotSpace
               | breControlEscape
               | breHexEscape
               | breUnicodeEscape
               | breLiteralEscape

breBackref           = /\\[1-9]/
breWordBoundaryAlias = /\\[<>]/
breWordBoundary      = /\\b/
breNonWordBoundary   = /\\B/
breClassDigit        = /\\d/
breClassNotDigit     = /\\D/
breClassWord         = /\\w/
breClassNotWord      = /\\W/
breClassSpace        = /\\s/
breClassNotSpace     = /\\S/
breControlEscape     = /\\[ntrfv0]/
breHexEscape         = /\\x[0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]/
breUnicodeEscape     = /\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{4}/
# Catch-all: `\X` for any non-special X. The exclusion list mirrors
# the rules above plus the structural escapes (`\(`, `\)`, `\|`,
# `\+`, `\?`, `\{`, `\}`) which must not be swallowed here — they're
# matched at a higher level by breGroup / breAltSep / breQuant*.
breLiteralEscape = /\\[^()|+?{}<>bBdDwWsSntrfv0xu1-9]/

# ─── Literal char ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Anything that's not a metacharacter consumed elsewhere. In BRE the
# unescaped metacharacters reduce to `.`, `*`, `^`, `$`, `[`, `\` —
# everything else is a literal. We exclude `\` so the escape rules
# above can claim it.
breLiteralChar = /[^.\\\[\^$*]/

# ─── Quantifier suffix ─────────────────────────────────────
# Order matters — `\{n,m\}` and `\{n\}` must be tried before bare
# `\+`/`\?` so the brace form isn't mis-tokenised mid-stream.
breQuantSuffix = breBraceQuant
               | breStarQ
               | breBackslashPlusQ
               | breBackslashQuestionQ

breStarQ              = "*"
breBackslashPlusQ     = /\\\+\??/
breBackslashQuestionQ = /\\\?\??/
# `\{n\}` or `\{n,m\}` or `\{n,\}`. Trailing `?` for non-greedy.
breBraceQuant         = /\\\{[0-9]+(?:,[0-9]*)?\\\}\??/

# POSIX Extended Regular Expressions.
#
# Modern unescaped convention — `(`, `)` group; `|` alternates; `+`,
# `?` quantify; `{n,m}` bounded. Backslash now ESCAPES specials to
# literal meaning (`\(` literal paren, `\|` literal pipe, `\+`
# literal plus). Backreferences `\1`-`\9` are POSIX-2008+.
#
# GNU extensions accepted: `\b`/`\B`, `\<`/`\>`, `\d`/`\w`/`\s` etc.
# POSIX character classes `[[:alpha:]]` work the same as in BRE.

ere = ereAlternation

ereAlternation = ereSequence + (ereAltTail)*
ereAltTail     = ereAltSep + ereSequence
ereAltSep      = "|"

ereSequence = (ereAtomQ)*

ereAtomQ = ereAtom + ereQuantSuffix?

ereAtom = ereGroup
        | ereCharClass
        | ereAnchorStart
        | ereAnchorEnd
        | ereDot
        | ereEscapedAtom
        | ereLiteralChar

ereGroup      = ereGroupOpen + ereAlternation + ereGroupClose
ereGroupOpen  = "("
ereGroupClose = ")"

# Same char-class regex shape as BRE. POSIX-class alternative listed
# first so `[[:alpha:]]` matches through both `]`s.
ereCharClass = /\[\^?\]?(?:\[:[a-z]+:\]|\\.|[^\]])*\]/

ereAnchorStart = "^"
ereAnchorEnd   = "$"
ereDot         = "."

ereEscapedAtom = ereBackref
               | ereWordBoundaryAlias
               | ereWordBoundary
               | ereNonWordBoundary
               | ereClassDigit
               | ereClassWord
               | ereClassSpace
               | ereClassNotDigit
               | ereClassNotWord
               | ereClassNotSpace
               | ereControlEscape
               | ereHexEscape
               | ereUnicodeEscape
               | ereLiteralEscape

ereBackref           = /\\[1-9]/
ereWordBoundaryAlias = /\\[<>]/
ereWordBoundary      = /\\b/
ereNonWordBoundary   = /\\B/
ereClassDigit        = /\\d/
ereClassNotDigit     = /\\D/
ereClassWord         = /\\w/
ereClassNotWord      = /\\W/
ereClassSpace        = /\\s/
ereClassNotSpace     = /\\S/
ereControlEscape     = /\\[ntrfv0]/
ereHexEscape         = /\\x[0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]/
ereUnicodeEscape     = /\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{4}/
# Catch-all `\X` for any X not already handled. Used by the model to
# escape ERE metacharacters back to literals (e.g. `\(` to get a
# literal paren).
ereLiteralEscape = /\\[^bBdDwWsSntrfv0xu1-9]/

# Literal char: anything that isn't an unescaped metacharacter or `\`.
ereLiteralChar = /[^.\\\[\^$()|+*?{}]/

# Order matters: try `{n,m}` first (longer match) before the bare
# operators.
ereQuantSuffix = ereBraceQuant
               | ereStarQ
               | erePlusQ
               | ereQuestionQ

ereStarQ      = /\*\??/
erePlusQ      = /\+\??/
ereQuestionQ  = /\?\??/
ereBraceQuant = /\{[0-9]+(?:,[0-9]*)?\}\??/

# PCRE-ish regex grammar. Superset of ERE with extra group/assertion
# forms. Unsupported PCRE features (recursive patterns `(?R)`,
# conditionals `(?(...)...)`, atomic groups `(?>...)`, possessive
# quantifiers, `\K`) are REJECTED by the visitor at AST-build time
# rather than by the grammar — the grammar accepts them syntactically
# so the visitor can produce a clear error message.

pcre = pcreAlternation

pcreAlternation = pcreSequence + (pcreAltTail)*
pcreAltTail     = pcreAltSep + pcreSequence
pcreAltSep      = "|"

pcreSequence = (pcreAtomQ)*

pcreAtomQ = pcreAtom + pcreQuantSuffix?

# Order matters — the more-specific group forms must precede the
# plain capturing group so `(?:...)` etc. aren't swallowed by it.
pcreAtom = pcreNonCapturingGroup
         | pcreNamedGroupJs
         | pcreNamedGroupPython
         | pcreLookahead
         | pcreNegativeLookahead
         | pcreLookbehind
         | pcreNegativeLookbehind
         | pcreUnsupportedSpecialGroup
         | pcreGroup
         | pcreCharClass
         | pcreAnchorStart
         | pcreAnchorEnd
         | pcreDot
         | pcreEscapedAtom
         | pcreLiteralChar

# Plain group `(...)`.
pcreGroup      = pcreGroupOpen + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose
pcreGroupOpen  = "("
pcreGroupClose = ")"

# `(?:...)` non-capturing.
pcreNonCapturingGroup = pcreNonCapOpen + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose
pcreNonCapOpen        = "(?:"

# `(?<name>...)` JS-style named group.
pcreNamedGroupJs    = pcreNamedJsOpen + pcreGroupName + ">" + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose
pcreNamedJsOpen     = "(?<"
pcreGroupName       = /[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*/

# `(?P<name>...)` Python-style named group — normalised by the visitor.
pcreNamedGroupPython = pcreNamedPyOpen + pcreGroupName + ">" + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose
pcreNamedPyOpen      = "(?P<"

# Lookaround: `(?=...)`, `(?!...)`, `(?<=...)`, `(?<!...)`.
pcreLookahead         = "(?="  + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose
pcreNegativeLookahead = "(?!"  + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose
pcreLookbehind        = "(?<=" + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose
pcreNegativeLookbehind = "(?<!" + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose

# Catch-all for unsupported `(?X...)` forms — listed so the grammar
# matches them but the visitor rejects with a clear message. Avoids
# falling through to `(` as a literal (which would be confusing) or
# to a parse error (less helpful than naming the feature). Matches
# from `(?X` through the next `)`. Body is any non-`)` chars so we
# don't try to balance nested parens (the unsupported forms don't
# nest in their common usage anyway).
pcreUnsupportedSpecialGroup = /\(\?[^:<=!P][^)]*\)/

pcreCharClass = /\[\^?\]?(?:\[:[a-z]+:\]|\\.|[^\]])*\]/

pcreAnchorStart = "^"
pcreAnchorEnd   = "$"
pcreDot         = "."

pcreEscapedAtom = pcreUnsupportedEscape
                | pcreBackref
                | pcreWordBoundaryAlias
                | pcreWordBoundary
                | pcreNonWordBoundary
                | pcreClassDigit
                | pcreClassWord
                | pcreClassSpace
                | pcreClassNotDigit
                | pcreClassNotWord
                | pcreClassNotSpace
                | pcreControlEscape
                | pcreHexEscape
                | pcreUnicodeEscape
                | pcreLiteralEscape

# `\K` and `\Q` are unsupported — match them so we can throw with a
# named error rather than swallow as `pcreLiteralEscape`.
pcreUnsupportedEscape = /\\[KQ]/

# Multi-digit backrefs (PCRE allows \10, \11, etc.).
pcreBackref           = /\\[1-9][0-9]?/
pcreWordBoundaryAlias = /\\[<>]/
pcreWordBoundary      = /\\b/
pcreNonWordBoundary   = /\\B/
pcreClassDigit        = /\\d/
pcreClassNotDigit     = /\\D/
pcreClassWord         = /\\w/
pcreClassNotWord      = /\\W/
pcreClassSpace        = /\\s/
pcreClassNotSpace     = /\\S/
pcreControlEscape     = /\\[ntrfv0]/
pcreHexEscape         = /\\x[0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]/
pcreUnicodeEscape     = /\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{4}/
pcreLiteralEscape     = /\\[^bBdDwWsSntrfv0xuKQ1-9]/

pcreLiteralChar = /[^.\\\[\^$()|+*?{}]/

pcreQuantSuffix = pcreBraceQuant
                | pcreStarQ
                | pcrePlusQ
                | pcreQuestionQ

# Possessive `*+`, `++`, `?+` are caught here so the visitor can
# reject them by name. JS RegExp can't express possessive
# quantifiers.
pcreStarQ     = /\*[?+]?/
pcrePlusQ     = /\+[?+]?/
pcreQuestionQ = /\?[?+]?/
pcreBraceQuant = /\{[0-9]+(?:,[0-9]*)?\}[?+]?/

# Whitespace/trivia between tokens — also consumes JavaScript-style comments
# (`// line` and `/* block */`), so comments are legal anywhere whitespace is.
# `ws` includes newlines; `lws` is same-line trivia (used where a newline is
# significant, e.g. after `return`).
ws = /(?:\s|\/\/[^\n]*|\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/)*/
lws = /(?:[ \t]|\/\/[^\n]*|\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/)*/
name = /(?!(while|for|if|else|else if|return|function|break|continue|this|class|constructor|private|new|var|const|let|try|catch|finally|throw|import|export|await|async|typeof)(?![a-zA-Z0-9_$]))[a-zA-Z_$][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*/

# Keywords. Each carries a trailing word-boundary (`(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])`) so it
# only matches as a WHOLE word — otherwise a keyword token would eat the prefix
# of an identifier (`new` in `newVal`, `this` in `thisThing`, `function` in
# `functionName`), mis-parsing it. (The `name` rule has the mirror guard for its
# own keyword exclusion.)
if = /if(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
else = /else(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
elseIf = /else if(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
while = /while(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
for = /for(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
const = /const(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
let = /let(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
func = /function(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
return = /return(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
break = /break(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
continue = /continue(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
this = /this(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
new = /new(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
typeof = /typeof(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
try = /try(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
catch = /catch(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
finally = /finally(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
throw = /throw(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
# Module system. `import`/`export` are RESERVED (they carry the same
# word-boundary guard as every other keyword AND appear in `name`'s exclusion
# list above, so `importedValue` is still an identifier while a bare `import` is
# not). `from`/`as` stay CONTEXTUAL — exactly as in JS, they remain legal
# identifiers and only read as keywords in the import positions below.
import = /import(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
export = /export(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
from = /from(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
as = /as(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/

# Syntax Chars
openBracket = "{"
closeBracket = "}"
openSqBracket = "[" 
closeSqBracket = "]"
openParen = "("
closeParen = ")"
colon = ":"
semiColon = ";"
comma = /\s*,\s*/
dot = "."
ellipsis = "..."
# Namespace-import wildcard (`import * as ns from …`). A separate token from the
# `mul` operator so the import rules never depend on arithmetic precedence.
star = "*"

# Operators 
gt = ">"
lt = "<"
gte = ">="
lte = "<="
# The arithmetic operators must NOT match when followed by `=`, or `out += x`
# parses as `out + (= x)` and stalls on the `=`. `additiveExpr` is tried before
# `assignmentExpr` in the `expr` alternation, so without this lookahead EVERY
# compound assignment (`+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`) is a syntax error — the tokens were
# declared and reachable, but the bare operator always won the race. Same class of
# fix as `===` vs `==`.
add = /\+(?!=)/
sub = /-(?!=)/
mul = /\*(?!=)/
div = /\/(?!=)/
exp = "**"
mod = "%"
# The 3-char forms MUST precede the 2-char ones in `equalityOperators` below, or
# `==` matches the first two characters of `===` and the parser stalls on the
# leftover `=` — which is exactly the error `1 === 1` used to produce.
seq = "==="
sne = "!=="
eq = "=="
ne = "!="
not = "!"
assign = "="
incr = "++"
decr = "--"
incrAssign = "+="
decrAssign = "-="
mulAssign = "*="
divAssign = "/="
and = "&&"
or = "||"
qm = "?"

assignmentOperators = assign | incrAssign | decrAssign | mulAssign | divAssign

# Types

# Number
number = /(?:Infinity|(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?)/
positive = add
negative = sub
sign = positive | negative

# String
doubleQuoteStringLiteral = /"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"/
singleQuoteStringLiteral = /'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'/
# Template literal — a backtick string with `${ expr }` interpolation, modeled
# on jq's interpolated string. `templateChunk` is a literal run (an escape
# `\X`, a `$` NOT opening `${`, or any char that isn't a backtick/backslash),
# and `templateInterpolation` recurses into `expr` between `${` and `}`. The
# self-reference sits in the MIDDLE (never at the start/end), so the Expression
# classifier treats the whole literal as an atom — same shape as a group.
templateChunk = /(?:\\[\s\S]|\$(?!\{)|[^`$\\])+/
templateInterpStart = /\$\{/
templateInterpolation = templateInterpStart + ws? + expr + ws? + closeBracket
templatePart = templateInterpolation | templateChunk
templateParts = (templatePart)+
templateLiteral = "`" + templateParts? + "`"
string = doubleQuoteStringLiteral | singleQuoteStringLiteral | templateLiteral

# Regex literal `/pattern/flags`. Lives in `value` (an ATOM), so cpat's
# Expression classifier only tries it where an operand is expected — a `/` in
# operator position stays division (`a / b`). The `(?![*/])` guard after the
# opening slash means `//…` (line comment) and `/*…` (block comment) are NEVER
# read as a regex (they're consumed by `ws`), and empty `//` isn't a regex. The
# body is one-or-more of: an escape `\X`, a char class `[...]` (so a `/` inside
# `[...]` doesn't close the literal), or any char that isn't `/`, `\`, or a
# newline. Flags are the JS-expressible set; `buildSayaRegExp` validates them.
regexLiteral = /\/(?![*\/])(?:\\[\s\S]|\[(?:\\[\s\S]|[^\]\\\n])*\]|[^\/\\\n])+\/[gimsuy]*/

# Boolean (word-boundary so `trueFlag`/`falsey` are identifiers, not literals)
true = /true(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
false = /false(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
boolean = true | false

# Null (word-boundary so `nullable`/`nullCheck` are identifiers, not the literal)
null = /null(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/

# Object Literal
propertyName = name
# A key may be a bare identifier OR a string literal (`{ "a-b": 1 }`). Both a
# `propertyName` and a string-literal node reduce to a SayaString whose `.value`
# is the key, so the `property` visitor handles either with no change.
propertyKey = propertyName | string
# A property is either `key: value` (propertyFull) or ES2015 shorthand — a bare
# identifier `{ a }` meaning `{ a: a }` (propertyShorthand; identifier-only, so
# no string/quoted shorthand). propertyFull is tried first (it needs the colon),
# so a bare name falls through to shorthand.
propertyFull = propertyKey + ws? + colon + ws? + expr
propertyShorthand = name
# Object spread `{ ...obj }` — merges the spread source's own properties. Tried
# first (it opens with `...`); later keys win over spread ones (visitor order).
objectSpread = ellipsis + ws? + expr
property = objectSpread | propertyFull | propertyShorthand
properties = (property, comma trim)+
objectLiteral = openBracket + ws? + properties? + ws? + comma? + ws? + closeBracket

# Array Literal
# Array spread `[ ...arr ]` — splices the spread source's elements in place.
arraySpread = ellipsis + ws? + expr
arrayLiteralItem = arraySpread | expr
arrayLiteralItems = (arrayLiteralItem, comma trim)+
# Committed at `[` (see groupExpr's note): nothing else in `expr` can start
# with a bare `[` — propertyAccess's bracket comes AFTER a value. Without the
# cut, `[[[[1` was the same exponential re-entry as the paren bomb
# (~x4 per character; 12 chars = 14s of parse).
arrayLiteral = openSqBracket ~/ ws? + arrayLiteralItems? + ws? + comma? + ws? + closeSqBracket

# function
paramName = name
paramWithDefaultValue = paramName + ws? + assign + ws? + expr
param = paramWithDefaultValue | paramName
params = (param, comma)+
functionSignature = openParen + ws? + params? + ws? + comma? + ws? + closeParen
functionName = name
function = func + ws? + functionName? + ws? + functionSignature + ws? + block

# Value
variableIdentifier = name
memberName = name
memberAccess = value + ws? + dot + ws? + memberName
propertyAccessName = string | number
propertyAccess = value + ws? + openSqBracket + ws? + expr + ws? + closeSqBracket
args = (expr, comma)+
invocation = value + ws? + openParen + ws? + args? + ws? + comma? + ws? + closeParen?

value =   invocation |
        memberAccess |
      propertyAccess |
              number |
              string |
        regexLiteral |
             boolean |
                null |
        arrayLiteral |
       objectLiteral |
       arrowFunction |
            function |
                this |
           groupExpr |
  variableIdentifier

# Arrow functions: `(a, b) => expr`, `(a, b) => { … }`, and the bare-param
# `x => x * 2`.
#
# The node is shaped like a `function` MINUS its name — `[params, body]` — so the
# existing `_invokeFunction` drives it unchanged. A concise body needs no implicit
# `return` either: `_invokeFunction` returns whatever processing the last child
# yields, and for an `expr` that is simply its value.
#
# `arrowBody` tries `block` before `expr` so `() => { … }` is a BLOCK, not an
# object literal — matching JS, where an object body needs `() => ({ … })`.
arrow = "=>"
arrowParams = functionSignature | paramName
arrowBody = block | expr
arrowFunction = arrowParams + ws? + arrow + ws? + arrowBody

# Expression
additiveOperators = add | sub
additiveExpr = expr + ws? + additiveOperators + ws? + expr

multiplicativeOperators = mul | div | mod
multiplicativeExpr = expr + ws? + multiplicativeOperators + ws? + expr

expExpr = expr + ws? + exp + ws? + expr

relationalOperators = gte | lte | gt | lt 
relationalExpr = expr + ws? + relationalOperators + ws? + expr

equalityOperators = seq | sne | eq | ne 
equalityExpr = expr + ws? + equalityOperators + ws? +  expr

logicalAndExpr = expr + ws? + and + ws? + expr
logicalOrExpr = expr + ws? + or + ws? + expr

assignmentExpr = expr + ws? + assignmentOperators + ws? + expr
# The `~/` commits the expression choice to the group once `(` is consumed.
# Safe because `arrowFunction` is listed BEFORE groupExpr in `expr` — an
# arrow's `(params) =>` has already had its chance by the time we get here,
# and no LATER alternative can start with `(`. Without the cut, a paren run
# like `((((1` re-entered `expr` at every depth through multiple paths —
# measured ~x5 per character (12 chars = 79s of parse; docs/cpu-runaway-audit.md K1).
groupExpr = openParen ~/ ws? + expr + ws? + closeParen

postfixOperators = incr | decr
postfixExpr = expr + ws? + postfixOperators
unaryOperators = incr | decr | not | add | sub
unaryExpr = unaryOperators + ws? + expr
# `typeof x`. Kept out of `unaryOperators` on purpose: that rule allows OPTIONAL
# whitespace before the operand, so `typeof` there would make `typeofx` parse as
# `typeof x`. A word operator must be followed by real separation, hence `ws`
# (required) rather than `ws?` — a parenthesised operand still works because
# `typeof(x)` has the group as its expr... which needs no space, so the group form
# is spelled with the space: `typeof (x)`.
typeofExpr = typeof + ws + expr
instantiation = new + ws? + expr

ternaryExpr = expr + ws? + qm + ws? + expr + ws? + colon + ws? + expr

expr =      postfixExpr |
             typeofExpr |
              unaryExpr | 
          expExpr right |
     multiplicativeExpr | 
           additiveExpr | 
         relationalExpr | 
           equalityExpr | 
         logicalAndExpr | 
          logicalOrExpr | 
            ternaryExpr |
         assignmentExpr |
          instantiation |
                  value

# Statements
functionStatement = function
variableName = name
# A declaration opens with `const` or `let` — both block-scoped (bound in the
# current frame). `var` is intentionally NOT supported (it stays reserved via
# the `name` exclusion, so `var x` fails loudly instead of mis-parsing). `const`
# is not enforced immutable. The keyword collapses out in cleanAst.
declarator = const | let
variableDeclarationStatement = declarator + ws? + variableName
variableAssignmentStatement = declarator + ws? + variableName + ws? + assign + ws? + expr
returnStatement = return + lws? + expr?
breakStatement = break
continueStatement = continue

# ── Module system ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# `import { a, b as c } from "./util.saya"` and `import * as util from "./util.saya"`.
#
# The specifier is a PLAIN quoted string — deliberately NOT `string`, which
# would also admit a template literal. Specifiers must be statically readable
# from the source (the module loader resolves them before any code runs), so an
# interpolated `` `./${dir}.saya` `` is a parse error rather than a silent
# runtime hole. This is also what keeps the private file map non-computable.
moduleSpecifier = doubleQuoteStringLiteral | singleQuoteStringLiteral

# `importAliased` is listed FIRST in `importBinding` so the LONGER match wins:
# cpat takes the first alternative that succeeds, so a bare `importName` would
# otherwise match `a` in `a as b` and leave `as b` dangling.
importName = name
importAlias = name
importAliased = importName + ws? + as + ws? + importAlias
importBinding = importAliased | importName
importBindings = (importBinding, comma)+
namedImports = openBracket + ws? + importBindings? + ws? + closeBracket
namespaceImport = star + ws? + as + ws? + importAlias
importClause = namedImports | namespaceImport
importStatement = import + ws? + importClause + ws? + from + ws? + moduleSpecifier

# `export function f() {}` / `export const x = 1` / `export let y`.
#
# A MODIFIER on an existing declaration rather than a new declaration form, so
# the underlying statement rules — and their visitors — are untouched: the
# `exportStatement` visitor runs its child declaration normally and then records
# the declared name on the module frame's export set.
exportable = functionStatement | variableAssignmentStatement | variableDeclarationStatement
exportStatement = export + ws? + exportable

# Branching
condition = groupExpr

# A control-flow BODY is either a `{ … }` block or a single unbraced statement, so
# `if (!city) return { … };` parses — the shape a JS author writes without thinking,
# and previously a bare "unexpected \"r\"" that cost a real agent two iterations.
#
# `loneStatement` wraps exactly ONE `statement`, never a list: `statements` is
# `(statement)+` and greedy, so using it here would let `if (x) a; b;` swallow `b`
# into the branch.
loneStatement = statement
body = block | loneStatement

elseBranch = else + ws? + body
elseIfBranch = elseIf + ws? + condition + ws? + body
elseIfBranches = (elseIfBranch, ws)+
ifStatement = if + ws? + condition + ws? + body + ws? + elseIfBranches? + ws? + elseBranch? 

# Loops
whileHeader = condition
whileStatement = while + ws? + whileHeader + ws? + body
forInit = variableAssignmentStatement | expr
forTest = expr
forUpdate = expr
forHeader = openParen + ws? + forInit? + ws? + semiColon + ws? + forTest? + semiColon + ws? + forUpdate? + ws? + closeParen 
forStatement = for + ws? + forHeader + ws? + body

# `for (const x of iterable)` and `for (const k in object)`.
#
# `of` and `in` stay CONTEXTUAL — they are not added to `name`'s exclusion list,
# so both remain legal identifiers and only read as keywords in these headers
# (JS does the same for `of`). The iterable/object is an `expr`, so
# `for (const x of items.filter(f))` works.
of = /of(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
in = /in(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
forEachTarget = declarator + ws? + variableName
forOfHeader = openParen + ws? + forEachTarget + ws? + of + ws? + expr + ws? + closeParen
forOfStatement = for + ws? + forOfHeader + ws? + body
forInHeader = openParen + ws? + forEachTarget + ws? + in + ws? + expr + ws? + closeParen
forInStatement = for + ws? + forInHeader + ws? + body

# Error handling
throwStatement = throw + ws? + expr
catchBinding = openParen + ws? + name + ws? + closeParen
catchClause = catch + ws? + catchBinding? + ws? + block
finallyClause = finally + ws? + block
tryStatement = try + ws? + block + ws? + catchClause? + ws? + finallyClause?

# Classes (word-boundary so `className`/`classify`/`privateKey` are identifiers)
private = /private(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
class = /class(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
constructor = /constructor(?![A-Za-z0-9_$])/
accessModifiers = private

classPropertyName = name

block = openBracket + ws? + statements? + ws? + closeBracket
allStatements = importStatement |
                           exportStatement |
                  variableAssignmentStatement |
               variableDeclarationStatement |
                            returnStatement |
                                ifStatement |
                             whileStatement |
                             forOfStatement |
                             forInStatement |
                               forStatement |

grammars.text:
# sed — script grammar.
#
# Input: the raw sed script text (the string the user passes as the
# first positional, e.g. `s/foo/bar/g;/baz/d`).
#
# Strategy: cpat captures the script's HIGH-LEVEL structure
# (statements, addresses, command letters, separators). The
# data-dependent bodies (`s/.../.../`, `y/.../.../`, `c TEXT`, etc.)
# are captured as opaque regex matches and unpacked by the visitor —
# the variable-delimiter problem doesn't fit a clean PEG and the
# visitor already needs to interpret the inner content (regex
# compilation, escape translation) regardless.
#
# For variable-delim commands we use JS regex NAMED BACKREFERENCES
# (`(?<d>.)...\k<d>`) — supported since ES2018. The first non-alpha
# non-whitespace char after `s` or `y` becomes the delimiter; the
# regex matches "any char or backslash-escape that isn't the
# delimiter, until the delimiter."

# ─── Whitespace + separators ────────────────────────────────
# Inline whitespace inside a statement (between address and command,
# around `,` in a range). NOT a statement separator.
ws = /[ \t]+/

# Statement separator — `;` or newline, any number of them.
sep = /[ \t]*[;\n][ \t;\n]*/

# ─── Address atoms ──────────────────────────────────────────
lineAddr = /\d+/
lastAddr = "$"
# Regex address: `/PAT/` where PAT can contain `\/` and other escapes
# but not unescaped `/` or `\n`.
regexAddr = /\/(?:\\.|[^\/\\\n])*\//

singleAddr = regexAddr | lastAddr | lineAddr

# ─── Range ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
comma = ","
rangeAddr = singleAddr + ws? + comma + ws? + singleAddr

# An address can be a range OR a single addr. Range listed first so
# cpat's PEG commits to the longer form when comma is present.
addressSpec = rangeAddr | singleAddr

# ─── Negation ──────────────────────────────────────────────
bang = "!"

# ─── Command bodies ────────────────────────────────────────
# Each body rule captures one complete command as its `node.value`.
# The visitor then peels apart pattern/replacement/flags or text.
#
# All body regexes are anchored to consume up to but not past the
# next statement boundary (`;` / `\n` / end of input) for atom
# commands; for `s` / `y` the regex naturally stops after the
# trailing delimiter and optional flags.

# s/PAT/REPL/[gimp][NUM][ w FILE]
# `(?<sd>...)` captures the delimiter; `\k<sd>` references it.
# Body chars: backslash-escape (any char) OR any char that's not the
# delimiter or backslash. Flag region after the trailing delimiter:
#   - letter flags `[gimp]`
#   - optional numeric NUM (replace only the Nth match)
#   - optional `w FILE` trailer (write pattern space on successful
#     substitute; FILE runs until `;` / `\n`)
# Visitor parses the flag region; we accept letter+digit flags in
# any order, and the visitor errors on unknown letters.
sCmd = /s(?<sd>[^A-Za-z0-9\s\\\n])(?:\\.|(?!\k<sd>)[^\\])*\k<sd>(?:\\.|(?!\k<sd>)[^\\])*\k<sd>[gimp0-9]*(?:[ \t]*w[ \t]+[^;\n]+)?/

# y/SRC/DST/ — like s but no flags.
yCmd = /y(?<yd>[^A-Za-z0-9\s\\\n])(?:\\.|(?!\k<yd>)[^\\])*\k<yd>(?:\\.|(?!\k<yd>)[^\\])*\k<yd>/

# c / a / i — text commands. The body runs to an unescaped `\n` and
# NOTHING ELSE ends it. `\X` (backslash + any char including newline)
# is consumed as one escape unit, so GNU's `c\\\n line2\\\n line3`
# multi-line continuation works — the trailing `\\\n` between lines
# stays inside the regex's `\\.` branch.
#
# A `;` is ORDINARY TEXT here, matching real sed: `1c foo; bar`
# inserts "foo; bar", and you cannot put another command after a
# c/a/i on the same line because the text swallows it. This used to
# exclude `;` and so rejected any body containing one — which is
# every non-trivial line of code. Two real runs died on it, both
# while rewriting a chunk of a script with `c\`, and the error
# ("could not parse script") pointed at the whole script and named
# nothing. Verified against BSD sed: escaped and bare semicolons in
# a `-f` script both insert the text verbatim.
changeCmd = /c(?:\\(?:.|\n)|[^\n\\])*/
appendCmd = /a(?:\\(?:.|\n)|[^\n\\])*/
insertCmd = /i(?:\\(?:.|\n)|[^\n\\])*/

# r / w — file-I/O commands. Body is a filename run, same shape as
# the text commands minus the multi-line continuation (filenames
# don't contain newlines). A `;` is part of the filename here too,
# for the same reason it is part of a c/a/i body: real sed reads the
# rest of the LINE as the name.
readCmd  = /r(?:\\.|[^\n\\])*/
writeCmd = /w(?:\\.|[^\n\\])*/

# Branch + label commands. Label names: identifier-shape. `b` and
# `t` accept an optional label; absent = "branch to end of script."
labelDecl = /:[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]*/
bCmd      = /b(?:[ \t]+[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]*)?/
tCmd      = /t(?:[ \t]+[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]*)?/
TCmd      = /T(?:[ \t]+[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]*)?/

# Atom commands — single letter, no body.
pCmd = "p"
dCmd = "d"
qCmd = "q"
nCmd = "n"
lCmd = "l"
eqCmd = "="

# Hold-space commands. Single uppercase/lowercase letters; cpat
# alternation will commit on the matching letter.
hCmd  = "h"
HCmd  = "H"
gCmd  = "g"
GCmd  = "G"
xCmd  = "x"

# Multi-line commands (D / N / P): read or operate on lines
# beyond the current one. N appends next input line; D deletes
# the first newline-terminated part and restarts the cycle; P
# prints the first newline-terminated part.
NCmd  = "N"
DCmd  = "D"
PCmd  = "P"

atomCmd = pCmd | dCmd | qCmd | nCmd | NCmd | DCmd | PCmd | lCmd | eqCmd
        | hCmd | HCmd | gCmd | GCmd | xCmd

# Block: `{ cmd; cmd; … }`. Inner script reuses the top-level
# `statements` rule, so blocks nest naturally.
openBrace  = "{"
closeBrace = "}"
block = openBrace + sep? + statements + sep? + closeBrace

# Order matters in this alternation: multi-char (regex-captured)
# bodies tried before the single-letter atoms so `s.../.../` doesn't
# get misread as the `s` alone-then-garbage. `block` tried first so
# `{` isn't mistaken for a stray atom.
commandBody = block
            | sCmd | yCmd
            | changeCmd | appendCmd | insertCmd
            | readCmd | writeCmd
            | labelDecl | bCmd | tCmd | TCmd
            | atomCmd

# ─── Statement ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# [address] [!] command
statement = addressSpec? + ws? + bang? + ws? + commandBody

# ─── Top level ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Named repeat to avoid cpat's anonymous-pattern wrapper (see the
# convention in `docs/bash-roadmap.md`). The visitor walks
# `script.children` looking for `statements`, then iterates that.
statements = (statement, sep trim)*
script = sep? + statements + sep?
